syllabus_metadata.title: Geography Syllabus for Ordinary Secondary Education
syllabus_metadata.subject: Geography

competences.main_competence: 1.0 Demonstrate mastery of the structure of the Earth
competences.specific_competence: 1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the origin and the structure of the Earth and earth systems

learning_activities.activity: (a) Describe the internal structure of the Earth (crust, mantle, core) and their major characteristics (location, size/thickness, density and gross composition)
teaching_learning_methods: Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm on the internal structure of the Earth
Group work: Assign students to design models and drawings to characterise the internal structure of the Earth
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The internal structure of the Earth is correctly described
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Relevant books, globe/models, environment, and flash with content on internal structure of the earth

learning_activities.activity: (b) Describe the main external Earth systems (Hydrosphere, Atmosphere and Biosphere)
teaching_learning_methods: Questions & Answers: Guide students to explain the main external earth systems
Field observation: Guide students to observe and discuss the hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere with cases from their communities
Independent library study: Organise students to examine the main external earth systems
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The external structure of the Earth is correctly described
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Relevant books, globe/models, environment, and relevant ICT tools, flash with content on external structure of the earth (atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere and cryosphere)

competences.main_competence: 2.0 Demonstrate mastery of basic skills and techniques in Geography
competences.specific_competence: 2.1 Demonstrate an understanding of the basic techniques of map and photograph interpretation

learning_activities.activity: (a) Describe the basic principles of reading and interpreting maps (key, symbols, north direction, margin/frame, scale map title, and contour patterns)
teaching_learning_methods: Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm the basic principles of reading and interpreting maps
Group Discussion: Guide students to discuss basic principles of reading and interpreting maps
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The basic principles of reading and interpretation of maps are clearly explained
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Maps, relevant books, and relevant ICT simulation tools

learning_activities.activity: (b) Reading and interpreting various type of maps and their importance (topographical and statistical map)
teaching_learning_methods: Case Study: Guide students to interpret and analyse various types of maps and their importance to the community
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The basic principles of reading and interpretation of maps are clearly explained
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Maps, relevant books, and relevant ICT simulation tools

learning_activities.activity: (c) Describe the basic concept of photograph in Geography (meaning, types, elements and uses)
teaching_learning_methods: Brainstorming: Guide students to brainstorm the meaning, types, elements and importance of photographs in Geography
Group Discussion: Guide students to discuss the basic uses of photographs in Geography
Guest Speaker: Invite resourceful persons (e.g., cartographer, photographer, camera man/woman) to share their experiences on uses of photographs
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The concept of photograph and its contents are clearly explained
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Relevant books and photographs (ground, vertical and oblique), magazine/newspapers, camera, and relevant ICT tools

learning_activities.activity: (d) Describe the basic principles of photograph interpretation (identifying foreground, middle ground and background, associating objects with geographical phenomena)
teaching_learning_methods: Question & Answers: Guide students to discuss basic principles of photograph interpretation
Group Discussion: Guide students to identify different parts of photographs, interpret them and make association with geographical phenomena
Case Study: Guide students to use photographs to interpret different cases of geographical phenomena
learning_activities.assessment_criteria: The basic principles of interpretation of photography are clearly described
learning_activities.suggested_resources: Relevant books on photographs, photographs (ground, vertical and oblique), magazine/newspapers, and relevant ICT tools
